## 2. In-Depth Case Studies & Production System Architecture

### Case Study 01: Infraly — Developer Form Backend & Lightweight Lead CRM
- **Live URL**: <https://infraly.online>
- **Source Code**: <https://github.com/nitindogra7/crm>
- **Tech Stack**: Next.js 16, Express 5, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Prisma ORM, Clerk Authentication, Tailwind CSS
- **The Problem**:
  Jamstack landing pages, portfolio sites, and micro-SaaS products lose valuable inbound customer leads when static mailto links fail, third-party form widgets break, or heavy enterprise CRMs introduce high pricing and complex webhook configurations.
- **The System Architecture**:
  1. Built a high-throughput Express 5 backend ingestion pipeline capable of parsing and storing burst form submissions.
  2. Implemented honeypot spam traps, strict Zod payload validation, and instant automated notification alerts.
  3. Engineered a responsive Next.js 16 management dashboard where site owners can view, organize, tag, and export incoming leads in real time.
  4. Utilized Prisma ORM with PostgreSQL for transactional reliability, database migrations, and relational data queries.
- **Measurable Business Outcomes**:
  - Sub-100ms API ingestion pipeline for form submissions.
  - 100% lead capture with zero dropped form leads across production web forms.
  - Zero-maintenance integration: client sites connect with a single POST endpoint.

### Case Study 02: GetMeChai — Creator Patronage & Community Platform
- **Live URL**: <https://get-me-chai-seven.vercel.app>
- **Source Code**: <https://github.com/nitindogra7/getMeChai>
- **Tech Stack**: Next.js App Router, React 19, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Razorpay Payment Gateway, Tailwind CSS
- **The Problem**:
  Content creators, writers, open-source developers, and independent builders in India face steep commission cuts, payout delays, and high currency conversion penalties on foreign creator donation sites.
- **The System Architecture**:
  1. Integrated Razorpay modern checkout with server-side webhook signature verification for instant payment confirmation and transaction reconciliation.
  2. Implemented relational database schema in PostgreSQL to manage user profiles, creator feeds, payment ledgers, and transaction histories.
  3. Leveraged Next.js Server Components, server actions, and optimistic UI patterns for sub-second feed updates and tipping reactions.
- **Measurable Business Outcomes**:
  - Frictionless, 1-click payment flow for supporters with zero drop-off.
  - 100% verified server-side transaction reconciliation via webhooks.
  - Responsive creator feeds that load in under 1 second on mobile networks.

### Case Study 03: LogoCraft — AI-Driven Vector Identity Generator
- **Live URL**: <https://logocraft.nitindogra.space/>
- **Source Code**: <https://github.com/nitindogra7/logoCraft>
- **Tech Stack**: React, Express.js, TypeScript, Hugging Face AI Diffusion Inference APIs, Credit Billing System
- **The Problem**:
  Early-stage startup founders and indie hackers need distinct, vector-quality logos and visual brand marks quickly without paying thousands of dollars or waiting weeks for traditional design agencies.
- **The System Architecture**:
  1. Engineered prompt enhancement pipelines translating basic brand names and keywords into high-contrast vector concepts.
  2. Connected Hugging Face AI diffusion inference models with server-side caching to optimize compute costs and generation times.
  3. Implemented a secure credit-based token accounting ledger allowing users to preview, purchase, and export brand assets in SVG and high-res PNG formats.
- **Measurable Business Outcomes**:
  - Average logo generation latency < 8 seconds.
  - Automated vectorization and high-resolution asset export.
  - Zero cloud GPU idle waste using on-demand serverless inference calls.

## 5. Technical Competencies & Framework Authority

- **Frontend**: Next.js 15/16 (App Router, Server Components, Server Actions, Partial Prerendering), React 19, TypeScript (Strict Mode), Tailwind CSS v4, Shadcn UI, Radix UI, Framer Motion, HTML5, CSS3.
- **Backend**: Node.js, Express.js (v5), RESTful API Design, GraphQL Basics, Webhook Ingestion, Server-Sent Events (SSE).
- **Databases & ORM**: PostgreSQL, Supabase, Prisma ORM, MongoDB, SQL schema design, migrations, indexing.
- **Authentication & Security**: Clerk Authentication, NextAuth / Auth.js, JWT (JSON Web Tokens), OAuth 2.0, RBAC, CSRF/CORS protection, Rate limiting.
- **Payments & Billing**: Razorpay integration, Stripe checkout & billing webhooks, credit/token accounting.
- **Cloud & DevOps**: Vercel deployment, Railway, Render, Git, GitHub Actions CI/CD, Docker fundamentals.
- **AI Integration**: OpenAI API, Anthropic Claude API, Hugging Face Diffusion Models, LangChain concepts, LLM prompt engineering.
- **Performance & SEO**: Core Web Vitals (LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1), Technical SEO, AEO, GEO, Schema.org JSON-LD graph generation, semantic HTML5.

## 8. Client & Recruiter FAQs

### Q: What is Nitin's availability for new projects or full-time roles?
A: Nitin is currently open to full-stack engineering roles, contract development contracts, and startup MVP builds. Inquiries receive replies within 24 hours.

### Q: How does Nitin collaborate across different time zones?
A: Nitin is based in New Delhi (UTC+5:30). He conducts real-time video standups during European mornings (CET) and US mornings (EST/PST), and maintains structured asynchronous communication via Slack, GitHub issues, and loom recordings for seamless handoffs.

### Q: Who owns the intellectual property and code?
A: 100% of the code, git history, database schemas, and intellectual property belong to the client upon milestone payment. Nitin delivers clean, documented repositories with zero vendor lock-in.

### Q: How are projects estimated and priced?
A: Fixed-scope projects receive a clear, milestone-based breakdown with defined deliverables and deadlines. Retainer agreements feature transparent weekly tracking.

### Q: Can Nitin assist with existing legacy codebases?
A: Yes. Nitin frequently audits and modernizes existing React or Next.js applications, resolving performance bottlenecks, upgrading legacy dependencies, and refactoring unstructured code into modular TypeScript architectures.
